skill.name: debugging-websocket-issues
skill.description: Diagnose Node.js WebSocket frame errors, conflicting upgrade handlers, compression mismatches, and raw HTTP written to upgraded sockets.
skill.summary: Diagnoses WebSocket frame errors through upgrade routing, compression checks, raw frame inspection, and targeted verification.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: All 38 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, TypeScript examples, JavaScript template literals, and diagnostic prose. The skill contains no prompt injection, shell execution, outbound requests, malicious intent, or data-exfiltration intent. Two contextual risks remain: malformed Host input can throw during upgrade routing, and raw frame logging can expose payload bytes.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated Host header parsing can raise an uncaught exception.
remediation.suggestion: Use a fixed local URL base, validate the pathname, and catch parsing errors before destroying the socket.

remediation.issue: Raw frame diagnostics may log sensitive payload bytes.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict instrumentation to controlled environments, redact payload bytes, and remove it after diagnosis.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Host Header Can Disrupt Upgrade Handling
semantic_findings.description: The routing example builds a URL from request.headers.host without validation or exception handling. A malformed Host header can throw inside the upgrade callback.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code passes an untrusted HTTP Host header into new URL without a try-catch. Node.js throws for malformed URL bases.

semantic_findings.title: Raw Frame Logging Can Expose Payload Data
semantic_findings.description: The diagnostic hook logs the first 20 raw bytes from each received chunk. Application frames may place sensitive payload bytes within that range.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The logging call is explicit, but exposure depends on payload content and where diagnostics run.

content.value_statement: WebSocket frame errors can hide conflicts between upgrade handlers or compression settings. This skill explains how to inspect frames, route upgrades, and verify fixes.
actual_capabilities: Maps common frame errors and close code 1006 to likely upgrade or compression causes.
Explains how competing WebSocketServer upgrade listeners can write HTTP data onto an upgraded socket.
Shows a single-listener pathname routing pattern with noServer mode.
Demonstrates temporary frame inspection and interpretation of FIN, RSV1, opcode, and HTTP byte signatures.
Provides a verification checklist for frame flags, extension headers, payload sizes, and repeated broadcasts.
limitations: Focuses on Node.js WebSocketServer behavior and may require adaptation for other runtimes or libraries.
Does not inspect a live server, browser, network trace, proxy, or deployment automatically.
Uses private socket internals for optional frame inspection, which can change between library versions.
Does not replace authentication, authorization, origin validation, rate limiting, or production monitoring.

use_cases.title: Resolve client frame errors
use_cases.description: Trace Invalid frame header or RSV1 errors from browser clients to server upgrade conflicts.

use_cases.title: Stabilize shared HTTP servers
use_cases.description: Route several WebSocketServer instances through one upgrade listener without competing handshake responses.

use_cases.title: Investigate production disconnects
use_cases.description: Interpret close code 1006 and raw frame bytes before changing compression or proxy settings.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a frame error
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this error: [paste error]. Identify the likely causes and give a short checklist using the skill guidance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a specific client or server error.

prompt_templates.title: Review upgrade routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these WebSocketServer definitions and upgrade listeners: [paste relevant code]. Find conflicts and describe the smallest routing change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare several endpoints sharing one HTTP server.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret frame evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these first-frame bytes and response headers: [paste observations]. Determine whether the client received HTTP, compressed data, or a valid frame.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use captured frame evidence to separate likely causes.

prompt_templates.title: Design an incident investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a diagnostic sequence for intermittent code 1006 failures across [number] WebSocket endpoints. Include evidence, hypotheses, isolation steps, and verification criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan an advanced investigation for intermittent production failures.

output_examples.input: The client reports RSV1 must be clear when two endpoints share one HTTP server.
output: Likely cause: two WebSocket servers process the same HTTP upgrade.
Recommended change: use one upgrade listener and route each pathname to one server.
Verification: confirm frames no longer begin with HTTP bytes and repeated connections remain stable.

output_examples.input: The first received bytes begin with hexadecimal 48545450 after a successful upgrade.
output_examples.output: Those bytes represent HTTP text, not a valid WebSocket frame. Check for a second upgrade listener that sends an HTTP rejection.

output_examples.input: The first byte sets RSV1, and the extension response does not include compression.
output_examples.output: The compression negotiation is inconsistent. Compare client and server extension settings, then retest with compression disabled to isolate the mismatch.

best_practices: Collect the exact client error, close code, upgrade headers, and first frame bytes before changing configuration.
Test each WebSocket endpoint alone, then together, to expose competing upgrade listeners.
Verify the fix with repeated connections, broadcasts, and frame inspection under realistic traffic.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every RSV1 error is a compression problem.
Do not attach several independent upgrade handlers to the same HTTP server without explicit routing.
Do not leave private socket instrumentation enabled in production after diagnosis.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides explanatory TypeScript examples and diagnostic guidance. You decide which changes or instrumentation to apply.

faq.question: Which WebSocket library does it cover?
faq.answer: The examples target Node.js and the ws library. The routing and frame concepts also apply to similar server implementations.

faq.question: Can it diagnose proxy problems?
faq.answer: It can help distinguish raw HTTP, compression, and server routing symptoms. It does not inspect proxy configuration automatically.

faq.question: Why does hexadecimal 48545450 matter?
faq.answer: It represents the ASCII letters HTTP. Seeing it at a frame boundary suggests an HTTP response reached an upgraded socket.

faq.question: Should compression always be disabled?
faq.answer: No. Disable it only to isolate negotiation problems or when your requirements permit. Validate client and server extension settings before deciding.

faq.question: Is private socket inspection safe for production?
faq.answer: Use it temporarily in controlled diagnostics. Private APIs can change, and frame logging may expose payload data or add overhead.
